articles.title: French thriller Jupiter brings nuclear anxiety to red carpets of Venice
articles.summary: Director Alexandre Smia says film about Russia detonating nuclear warhead – and US refusing to respond – is not unrealistic. Russia has detonated a nuclear warhead over the Black Sea to underline its desire to revenge an assassination attempt on the Russian president.
body: A new thriller, which has brought nuclear anxiety to the red carpets of the Venice film festival this week, plays through what would happen next. In Jupiter, which premiered on the Lido on Friday, the duty to square up to the Kremlin and enter the stress-inducing mind games of the nuclear deterrent falls on the fictional French president Paul Archambault (played by the hulking French actor Denis Ménochet), who is backed in his mission by the British prime minister.
It’s a scenario that is far from unrealistic, the French film-maker Alexandre Smia said on the eve of his film’s premiere.

“Even if the US disengagement from Nato is not official, we have reason to doubt that the US would offer its nuclear umbrella if one European city were to be attacked nowadays,” said Smia, who has previously directed episodes of the French spy TV series Le Bureau des Légendes.

“And considering that France is the only country in Europe that is both a member of the European community, of the security council of the United Nations and of Nato, it naturally becomes actually the country where the responsibility of making decisions lies.”

articles.title: Susan Sarandon Says She’s ‘Still Had Movies Taken Away Recently’ Over Palestine Support: ‘There Are Agencies That Are Telling People Not to Hire Me’
articles.summary: Susan Sarandon said she’s “still had movies taken away recently” over her outspoken support of Palestine. At the Venice Film Festival press conference for her new film “The Echo Chamber” on Sunday, Sarandon was asked if she thinks the narrative is changing in Hollywood when it comes to the conflict…
body: “I’ve still had movies taken away recently because there are agencies that are telling people not to hire me still,” she continued. “But that’s the power structure. I think within the people, certainly internationally, I feel welcome.”

“The Echo Chamber” hails from Italian director Andrea Pallaoro and filmed in Italy and Belgium. Sarandon stars in the romantic drama, which was Bernardo Bertolucci’s final screenplay, alongside Luca Marinelli and Alicia Vikander.
Sarandon said that Pallaoro was told not to work with her but did so anyway. “I thank Andrea for that, because he doesn’t listen to the warnings,” she said.

“There has been a change in terms of the general public, but there are still positions in my industry that are held by Zionists who have not relaxed their feelings towards me,” Sarandon concluded. “But I found my family, I found my people and I’m OK.”

articles.title: ‘Woman Unknown’ Director May el-Toukhy Talks the Torment of World War II ‘Horizontal Collaborators’ and Venice’s Female Director Snub: ‘It’s a Structural Problem’
articles.summary: In “Woman Unknown,” May el-Toukhy takes a closer look at women accused of having relationships with German soldiers during World War II. “When we started to build a story about a ‘horizontal collaborator,’ we realized that, during and after the war, the female body became part of national identity.
body: “You can find very similar stories that are thousands of years old. The shaving of a woman’s hair or her public shaming for ‘sharing’ her body is a very old concept. Even today, it’s still happening in many armed conflicts.”
Still, this suffering tends to be ignored by historians. The title of her film references that silence as well.

“I was inspired by Belarusian writer Svetlana Alexievich who wrote ‘The Unwomanly Face of War.’ She gathered these testimonies from women who talked about having their periods in war zones, hiding in sheds, and giving birth. It’s rare to have such recollections of the female experience during or after the war,” says el-Toukhy.

For Marie, a housemaid and a nanny, the future looks bright: she’s about to marry her wealthy employer. But in the weeks leading up to liberation in 1945, she must do her best to survive and ensure that her secrets don’t catch up with her.

“When we started to build a story about a ‘horizontal collaborator,’ we realized that, during and after the war, the female body became part of national identity.

It’s rare to have such recollections of the female experience during or after the war,” says el-Toukhy.

Maisie Williams has dabbled in witchcraft exactly once.
body: “It didn’t work, and that was where my days of witchcraft ended,” she adds, breaking into an infectious cackle.

The spell may not have worked that time, but Williams will soon try her own hand at witchcraft on screen in Practical Magic 2. The sequel to the beloved 1998 romcom, about two supernatural sisters played by Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman, it features Williams as Antonia, the youngest daughter of Bullock’s Sally Owens. She never did get her money back from her Etsy witch. “It was maybe, like, £16.50? Which is not going to break the bank, but good for her. Good for her, to be making money doing nothing!” Williams laughs again.

articles.title: ‘From Inside Out – The Architecture of Peter Zumthor’ Review: Wim Wenders’ Latest 3D Documentary Is an Architectural Marvel
articles.summary: The screen is usually a canvas, but it becomes a window to an enormous room in Wim Wenders’ latest 3D documentary, “From Inside Out – The Architecture of Peter Zumthor.” Within that room unfolds the tale of the Swiss architect of the title, told in occasionally laborious ways.
body: The German filmmaker trains his stereoscopic lens on the buildings of the Swiss architect, revealing them in surprising ways.

We eventually meet Zumthor in the present: an unassuming man in his eighties, whose descriptions of form, function and fluidity often repeat themselves, but whose sincerity and wisdom are hard to shake. As the film explores houses, museums and other Zumthor commissions, the architect’s use of light and natural materials becomes as important as the theoretical people he intends to fill each space — or, in the case of complicated restorations, the people who inhabited them decades ago. Wenders depicts these ghosts of past and future through dramatizations of curious travelers, whose whispering voiceover offers scattered thoughts on where they stand.

articles.title: Cristian Mungiu Is Glad You’re Arguing About ‘Fjord.’ Just Don’t Assume His Politics
articles.summary: The Romanian auteur is on the cusp of his Oscars breakthrough for his Cannes-winning social drama, which has already been hotly debated on social media for months: "People...assume that what the film says is the opinion of the filmmaker, and what the characters say is the truth. Come on."
body: We may have reached that moment. Just as the Academy has globalized at a rapid rate, in terms of both membership and recognition, Mungiu has roared back onto the scene with Fjord, which examines the infuriating and subtly tragic fallout of a conservative Romanian family’s move to Norway after their customs — from religiosity to parenting style — are skeptically interrogated by their new progressive government. Starring Oscar nominees Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve as the controversial parents in question, Fjord won the Palme d’Or in May, its backing by the great Cannes-to-Oscars whisperer that is Neon signaling a fruitful fall awards run.

articles.title: TV presenter among 12 sentenced to death in Egypt drugs case
articles.summary: Sarah Khalifa is best known for her TV programme Mission Impossible which dealt with crime issues.
body: Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa and 11 other people have been sentenced to death by hanging after being convicted of drugs charges.
According to state-owned al-Ahram newspaper, they were part of a criminal gang which imported ingredients used to make drugs with the intent of selling them.
Nine fellow defendants have been sentenced to life imprisonment, while seven have been acquitted.
However, it was only confirmed a month later after the court obtained a religious opinion from the grand mufti of Egypt - a legal requirement in death sentence cases.

articles.title: Oscars: Iraq picks ‘No Paradise If You Are Killed by a Woman’ as Best Intl. Feature Contender
articles.summary: Halkawt Mustafa’s feature, which premieres out of competition in Venice, follows a female Kurdish sniper who returns to Mosul to try and rescue her younger sister.
body: Iraq has selected No Paradise If You Are Killed by a Woman from Norwegian-Kurdish director Halkawt Mustafa as its official submission for the 2027 Oscar race in the Best International Feature category.
The film was the unanimous pick of Iraq’s official National Selection Committee for the Academy Awards, mandated by the state ministry of culture.

Mustafa, who was born in Iraqi Kurdistan and fled to Norway as a child, said the film was inspired by his encounter with a female Peshmerga sniper during the 2014 frontline battles, as female Kurdish fighters countered Islamic State attacks.

The director’s previous films include Hiding Saddam Hussein, a documentary about the farmer who hid the Iraqi dictator for 235 days in 2003, Iraq’s 2016 Oscar submission The Classic, and the 2015 documentary The Women ISIS Fears, which also looked at the world of female Kurdish fighters.

articles.title: Boy band star swaps stage for racecourse
articles.summary: JJ Hamblett is taking part in a charity horse race at Doncaster Racecourse on 11 September.
body: A former X Factor contestant and boy band member says his return to horse racing feels like a full-circle moment as he swaps the stage for the racecourse.
Before finding fame with pop group Union J, JJ Hamblett, who grew up in Newmarket in Suffolk, spent his youth horse racing and gained his jockey licence at 16.
His first competitive appearance came at Doncaster Racecourse in 2005 and on 11 September, he will return there to take part in The Leger Legends race.
"It's like I've done this huge 360 and gone back to where I started, which is going to be very unusual next week," said the 38-year-old.

articles.title: 30 Years Ago Today: Adam Sandler Made One Of The Worst Buddy Cop Movies Ever Made
articles.summary: Adam Sandler has starred in some of the greatest comedy films of all time, but also some of the worst. This one from 30 years ago is firmly in the latter camp.
body: Adam Sandler's best movies are some of the most beloved comedies of the last few decades. His bad movies? They're some of the worst comedies ever made, and I think it's fair to say even the man himself knows that. For every "Punch-Drunk Love" and "Hustle," there's a "Ridiculous 6" or "Pixels." Sandler is also responsible for one of the worst movies ever made, having produced the lousy Dana Carvey vehicle "The Master of Disguise," which to this day maintains a 1% critic score on Rotten Tomatoes (turns out one critic at Long Island Press liked it). At least Sandler can claim that his 1996 buddy cop effort "Bulletproof" beat "The Master of Disguise" by a whole seven percentage points.
